stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan impact: 20 flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to bad weather
stories.title: Cyclone Akvan impact: 20 flights cancelled at Ranchi airport due to bad weather
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Ranchi: As many as 20 flights were cancelled at the Birsa Munda Airport here on Saturday due to inclement weather triggered by cyclone 'Akvan', an official said.
Jharkhand has been experiencing cloudy weather coupled with light rain since Friday under the influence of the cyclone.
For safe landing or take-off, a visibility between 1,200 and 1,500 metres is required.
"The visibility at Ranchi airport was around 1,000 metres until 1pm," Airport Director Vinod Kumar told PTI.
In all, 20 scheduled flights were cancelled due to bad weather, including six Air India Express flights, an airport official said.
In addition, four flights were diverted due to inclement weather.
The state's weather is likely to improve from Sunday with clearing of clouds, an IMD official said.
"We are expecting the weather to improve from Sunday with dense fog in the morning hours.
A clear sunshine is likely from November 23," Baburaj PP, director at Ranchi Meteorological Centre, told PTI.
Chaibasa Sadar in West Singbhum district recorded highest rainfall at 34.4 mm during the past 24 hours till 8.30am on Saturday.
Ghatsila in East Singhbhum district registered 32.6 mm rainfall, Simega 28.2mm, Jamshedpur 22.2 mm and Ranchi recorded 12.4 mm rainfall.

The maximum temperature is likely to remain unchanged for the next 24 hours in the state and thereafter it will start rising by 6 degree Celsius during the next three days, according to the weather bulletin.

stories.headline: Skill development linked to national security, defence production: Rajnath Singh
stories.title: Skill development linked to national security, defence production: Rajnath Singh
stories.summary: Lucknow, Nov 21: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday said skill development is no longer limited to generating employment and is crucial for nation-building and national security, citing the example of India's growing defence production sector. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation here, Singh said the country's industries are expanding, and the nature of employment is undergoing transformation, making it essential for young people to continuously upgrade their skills. "Today, the importance of skill development is not limited to securing employment. It is connected with nation-building and national security. An important example of this is our defence production," he said. Singh said under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, industries are growing, and the methods of working are changing rapidly. "In such a situation, merely acquiring skills is not enough. It is also extremely important to keep up with the times. Therefore, our government is making efforts to ensure that skills of young people develop continuously through skilling, reskilling and upskilling initiatives," he said. The defence minister said the economic strength of a country is determined not merely by its natural resources, capital or technological advancement but also by the capabilities and skills of its citizens. "In our tradition, we have learnt that knowledge gives a person understanding, skills give them capability, and a combination of both makes them self-reliant," he said. Singh said the National Skill Convocation has helped change the perception that convocation ceremonies are associated primarily with universities and higher academic degrees. "Skill development is in no way inferior to formal education. Rather, it supplements and complements it," he asserted. Highlighting the expansion of the country's skill development ecosystem over the past 12 years, Singh said more than 1.64 crore young people have received training under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) till June 2026. He said the number of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) in the country has increased from approximately 9,800 in 2014 to more than 14,000 at present. However, he said, the significance of these figures lay in the transformation that skill development had brought to the lives of young people. "When a young person from a small town or village receives training from an ITI and starts working in an industry, they do not merely earn a livelihood but also transform the economic condition of their family," he said. Similarly, a young person who establishes an enterprise using technical skills not only creates employment for themselves, but also generates opportunities for others, contributing to the goal of self-reliance, he added. Singh said a strong skill ecosystem has been made possible through the vision of Prime Minister Modi, who recognised that skills need to be developed in mission mode to realise the goal of a developed India. He said skill development has progressed at an unprecedented pace over the past 12 years. Singh also congratulated the 52 national-level toppers from Industrial Training Institutes, National Skill Training Institutes and Institutes of Training of Trainers who were felicitated by Prime Minister Modi at the ceremony. He said the fifth National Skill Convocation is a special occasion as it is being held outside Delhi for the first time. Congratulating Union Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Jayant Chaudhary for organising the national-level programme in Lucknow, Singh also described it as a matter of pride for Uttar Pradesh and congratulated Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. The event was attended by Narendra Modi, Yogi Adityanath, Jayant Chaudhary and other senior dignitaries and officials. Singh, who represents Lucknow in the Lok Sabha, earlier welcomed the prime minister to the Uttar Pradesh capital and extended his greetings to young achievers who had arrived from different parts of the country.

stories.headline: Bulgarian FM lauds India's role in Black Sea peace efforts
stories.title: Bulgarian FM lauds India's role in Black Sea peace efforts
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 21 : Bulgaria's Foreign Minister Velislava Petrova-Chamova on Saturday lauded India's efforts to find a long-term solution to the security situation in the Black Sea region, saying it would help safeguard the movement of essential commodities, including food grains, fertilisers and oil. In her opening remarks during a meeting with External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar in New Delhi, Petrova highlighted Bulgaria's role in ensuring the safety of Indian seafarers affected by the escalation of the conflict in the region, involving search and rescue operations. “What one other aspect that really connects us is what we've seen with the escalation of the war in the Black Sea and the security environment that we are part of. It has affected, unfortunately, some of the Indian crew members, and our country has done our best to conduct successful search and rescue and to protect the crew as much as we can,” the Bulgarian FM said. “But of course, we really welcome your efforts in finding a long-term solution there, and very happy to work together with you to find a resolution that not only would improve the security situation there, but also would help those who are in need of the key food and grain products in this case, but also fertilizers, oil, any other products that are needed, and that are at risk because of the harder security situation in the Black Sea,” she added. Highlighting that her visit comes after a gap of 17 years since a Bulgarian Foreign Minister last visited India, Petrova said that this reflected a strong commitment to giving fresh impetus to bilateral relations and strengthening cooperation in multilateral forums. She also welcomed the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement (FTA), describing it as a huge achievement and expressing optimism about the opportunities it could create for trade and investment. “We really welcome this and are looking forward to what it is. It was a huge achievement, and I'm glad to say I met with some of your colleagues who worked on this on your side as well. And I was happy to see the commitment to put it into action. It will be important for Europe,” the Bulgarian FM stated. “For us in Bulgaria, as a country that is situated in a way as a gateway to Europe, this could be an opportunity for multiple new interactions, new business relationships, new investments on both sides as well, and ways in which we step on our bilateral relation that historically we've had,” she noted. ( IANS)

stories.headline: CJI Surya Kant calls for guidelines on AI use, disclosure in legal research
stories.title: CJI Surya Kant calls for guidelines on AI use, disclosure in legal research
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Saturday urged the Commonwealth Legal Education Association (CLEA) to develop model guidelines on the disclosure of AI assistance in legal research. Delivering the inaugural address at CLEA 1st Annual International Conference on Legal Education 2026 here, he also suggested that a minimum period of legal aid work be made compulsory for every student to graduate, with additional credits for those who go beyond it. "I would urge CLEA to take the lead by developing model guidelines on the disclosure of AI assistance in legal research, which law schools and journals across the Commonwealth could adapt to their own needs," he said. Talking about research in the age of AI, he cautioned that no student should be held guilty of misconduct on the word of a machine alone as software that claims to tell whether a given essay was written by a student or by a machine can go wrong for different reasons. stories.headline: Centre sanctions additional 25 companies of CAPF for Tripura municipal elections
stories.title: Centre sanctions additional 25 companies of CAPF for Tripura municipal elections
stories.summary: With local availability of CAPF personnel, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed for election duties; the deployment will continue even for a few days after the declaration of results on December 2
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Union Home Ministry has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of the Central Armed.
Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the elections of the urban local body elections in Tripura slated for November 27.
State Election Commissioner Pradip Chakraborty said the Home Ministry has informed the State government of its decision on Saturday (November 21, 2026).
He said with local availability of the CAPF personnel, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed for election duties.
The deployment will continue even for a few days after the declaration of results on December 2.

Opposition CPI(M) and Congress have long been demanding adequate deployment of the Central forces after voicing allegations that the ruling BJP is trying to make the elections a farce through gross irregularities and the use of government machinery.
They accused the State police of failing to discharge its duties neutrally.
The State Election Commission had announced a schedule to hold elections for 21 ULBs including Agartala Municipal Corporation.
However, the Congress and CPI(M), citing security and widespread threats, were restrained from filing nomination papers for five civic bodies.
Thus, the BJP has secured victory in these five ULBs unopposed and the polls will technically occur in 16 areas instead of 21.
Meanwhile, the election campaign has picked up pace with the countdown beginning for polling.
Opposition parties have alleged that their supporters are facing obstacles and threats during the door-to-door campaign.

stories.headline: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears 15 lakh free sites, one lakh houses
stories.summary: The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19

article_sentences: The Karnataka Cabinet has approved the distribution of 15 lakh free residential sites to landless families and construction of one lakh houses during 2026-27 at an estimated cost of ₹2,241 crore.
The decisions were taken at the Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on November 19.
The initiatives aim to provide housing security to families without residential sites and those unable to afford house construction.
Under the proposed Bhooguarantee scheme of the Karnataka government, the first phase will cover five lakh sites at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.

The government plans to develop nine lakh sites in rural areas, requiring around 45,000 acres, while five lakh urban beneficiaries will be accommodated through a G+3 housing model, according to a press release.
The government has identified 23,500 acres of government land across 31 districts, sufficient for about 4.70 lakh sites.
District administrations have been asked to identify additional land.
The first-phase development cost is estimated at ₹20,000 per site.
The proposed Niveshana Yojane will provide sites to eligible landless families, including ex-servicemen, with a 3% reservation for former defence personnel.
Priority will also be given to senior citizens, widows, divorced persons, single mothers, persons with disabilities and transgender persons.
The proposed reservation includes 19.5% for Scheduled Castes and 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes.
The Chief Minister has also directed officials to provide for reservation for Backward Classes.
